newsitem.title: UK: Arb shipping of oil prods perturbs vessel owners.
newsitem.headline: Arb shipping of oil prods perturbs vessel owners.

text.p: More arbitrage trading of oil products between regions is making vessel movements harder to predict for tanker owners, according to an owners survey.

"An increasing part of the trade is arbitrage trade due to price differentials and seasonal variations, and a declining part is traded due to lack of refinery capacity in certain areas and surpluses in others," Intertanko said in its July market report.
The Oslo-based tanker owners' organisation said strong relations between charterers and operators in some regions was causing volatility in the smaller spot market sector.
Spot rates were sometimes moving in opposite directions in different trades at the same time, it said.

South Korea, which increased oil product imports between 1986 and 1996 has now become a net exporter, with cargoes of mainly 30,000 tonnes moving to south China, Japan and to a lesser extent Taiwan, Intertanko quoted broker SSY as reporting.
Intertanko added that it had recorded 27 time charters of one year and above so far in 1997 for clean product tankers. Rates varied from $12,350 to $17,500 with an average of $14,380 a day, it said.
